entities.name: Jeongjong of Joseon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jeongjong of Joseon (Yi Bang-gwa, later Yi Gyeong; r. 1398–1400), the second monarch of the Joseon Dynasty, served as a pivotal, albeit largely ceremonial, transitional figure during a tumultuous period of dynastic consolidation. Born in 1357, the second son of King Taejo, the dynasty's founder, his brief reign was marked less by his own initiatives and more by the intense power struggles among his younger brothers, particularly the ambitious Yi Bang-won (later King Taejong). His ascent followed the First Strife of Princes in 1398, a bloody coup orchestrated by Yi Bang-won, which saw the assassination of two of Jeongjong's half-brothers and the effective sidelining of his father, King Taejo.

During his two-year tenure, Jeongjong's primary role was to stabilize the royal court and legitimize the shift of power towards Yi Bang-won, who held the real authority as Prince Regent. Reluctant to engage in the brutal factionalism, Jeongjong moved the capital back to Gaegyeong from Hanyang (modern Seoul) in 1399, a symbolic gesture intended to distance himself from the recent bloodshed in the new capital. He oversaw minor administrative reforms, but his reign was largely overshadowed by the ongoing machinations of his brothers. The Second Strife of Princes in 1400, another conflict involving Yi Bang-won, ultimately solidified the latter's claim to the throne, prompting Jeongjong's abdication just months later.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jeongjong's transitional reign was crucial for the early Joseon Dynasty, as his abdication facilitated the consolidation of power under King Taejong, thereby averting further large-scale civil conflict and establishing a more stable foundation for the new kingdom.
